title: How to Improve your Vibe Coding — Ian Butler
talk_summary: Ian Butler presents benchmark results showing popular coding agents have very low true-positive rates and high false-positive rates when finding bugs, causing alert fatigue. He offers three practical mitigations: bug-focused rules files, deliberate context management, and preferring thinking models.

takeaways.technique: Bug-focused rules file with explicit bug classes
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of vague 'find bugs' prompts, they supply scoped rules naming specific bug classes (auth bypass, SQL injection, protocol pollution) and OWASP Top 10 to prime the model toward those issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Be like, 'Hey cursor, I want you to examine my repository for off bypasses or protocol pollution, um SQL injection'
takeaways.numbers: Cursor had a 97% false positive rate over 100+ repos and 1,200+ issues; 3 of 6 agents had <=10% true positive rate out of 900+ reports

takeaways.technique: Require fix validation via tests in rules
takeaways.what_they_do: Rules instruct the agent that it must write and pass tests before changes enter the codebase, forcing verification of claimed fixes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to write and get tests to pass before this is coming into the codebase. You have to ensure they've actually fixed the bugs.

takeaways.technique: Feed diffs and preserve key files from compaction
takeaways.what_they_do: They manage context manually: pass diffs of changed code so the agent understands cause/effect, and prevent key files from being summarized out of the window during compaction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make sure you're feeding uh you know either diffs of the code uh that was changed to the agent... key files aren't being summarized

takeaways.what_they_do: Ask the agent to first produce an inventory of classes, variables, and usages across the codebase, then use that index to find bugs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: asking agents to come up with a uh step-by-step component inventory of your code... it becomes much more able to find bugs

takeaways.what_they_do: They observed thinking/reasoning models find deeper bugs than non-thinking models and recommend reaching for them for review tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: thinking models were significantly better um at finding bugs in a codebase... try to reach for thinking models

takeaways.technique: Run-to-run variability means single-pass review is unreliable
takeaways.what_they_do: They found the topline bug count stayed similar across runs but the specific bugs found changed each run, so agents never holistically inspect a file; they flag this as a limitation requiring multiple runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the topline number of bugs found would remain the same but they would actually the bugs themselves would change runto run
